title: Ang 870–875: Gond's Bhagats
hookLine: Kabir's elephant, and Namdev and Ravidas
tomorrow: some read Sanskrit, some count beads. what does Guru Nanak know?

lines: A MAN TIED AND THROWN DOWN.
cards: Videos of animals refusing to do what they're told are their own corner of the internet: the dog that won't leave a friend, the horse that stops at the edge. Kabir's hymn on ang 870 has an older one.
An elephant is driven at a man who's been tied up and thrown down. It's a frightening scene, and it ends gently.

teach.b: In paraphrase, Kabir sings: they tied my arms, bundled me up, and threw me down. The elephant was struck on the head to drive it on. But it ran off, trumpeting: I'm a sacrifice to this form of the Lord.
The judge shouted at the driver to force it forward. It wouldn't move. It stood as if in meditation, Kabir says, because the Lord lived in its heart.

Then it bowed to the bundled man, again and again. So the question for today: when power comes at someone who can't fight back, what protects them? Kabir's answer: the Lord within, even within the elephant.
In the Qur'an, the surah called The Elephant opens, in Pickthall's words: "Hast thou not seen how thy Lord dealt with the owners of the Elephant?"

It goes on to say God sent flocks of birds against that army and brought their plan to nothing. Shared: an elephant sent to crush people who couldn't stop it, and God who does. And one honest difference.

teach.h: A NEIGHBOR: THE SURAH OF THE ELEPHANT.
teach.b: In the surah, the elephant belongs to the attackers, and the answer comes from outside, from the sky.

teach.h: ONE FROM INSIDE, ONE FROM THE SKY.
teach.b: In Kabir's hymn, the answer comes from inside the elephant: the Lord lives in its heart, and it bows.
Two scriptures, two pictures of rescue, side by side. After Kabir, Namdev and Ravidas close Gond in devotion.

how: Kabir's hymn of the elephant (ang 870) is sung in kirtan in raga Gond; Sikh tellings tie it to a time Kabir was persecuted for his teaching.

o: where Guru Arjan's hymns in raga Gond end
where Kabir's hymns in raga Bilaval begin
where the Bhagats' hymns in raga Gond begin

p: tied and thrown before the elephant

s: in Kabir's hymn, the elephant tramples him
it runs off trumpeting, then bows to him again and again.
the Qur'an has a surah named for an elephant
in Pickthall: 'the owners of the Elephant.'
Kabir's hymn and the surah tell the same story
both stop an elephant sent to crush; in one God sends birds, in the other the elephant itself bows.

games.q: a friend of another faith says your two scriptures 'basically tell the same elephant story.' what's the fairest reply?
o: they share a rescue from an elephant, pictured differently, and both pictures matter.
they're the same story; the differences are just small details.
they have nothing in common; scriptures shouldn't be put side by side.
games.why: shared: an elephant sent against the defenseless, and God who stops it. different: birds from the sky in the surah; in Kabir, the Lord inside the elephant.

practice: Lower your head slowly, the way the elephant bowed, until your chin nearly rests on your chest. Let your shoulders soften with it and stay there for the sit, then rise slowly. If you'd like, read Kabir's hymn on ang 870 first.
